title: Frying
description: Cooking food in oil or fat
wiki_lead:
Frying is a method of cooking where food is made in oil or animal fat. Frying is believed to have first appeared in Ancient Egypt around 2500 BC, with tiger nut cakes deep fried in oil. 
A variety of foods can be fried. The amount of oil or fat will usually affect the food's taste and texture. Foods fried in more oil, or deep fried, will typically be crispier or more tender, whereas foods fried in less oil, like shallow frying or pan frying, will usually still be crisp but to a lesser extent. Other methods utilize the movement of the food in the pan or using oil or fat with other sauces. 
Frying is a dehydration process which involves the transfer of mass and heat. Different chemical changes take place during the frying process such as protein denaturation, starch gelatinization, surface browning, rapid water evaporation and oil absorption.
wiki_excerpt:
Frying is a method of cooking where food is made in oil or animal fat. Frying is believed to have first appeared in Ancient Egypt around 2500 BC, with tiger nut cakes deep fried in oil. 
A variety of foods can be fried. The amount of oil or fat will usually affect the food's taste and texture. Foods fried in more oil, or deep fried, will typically be crispier or more tender, whereas foods fried in less oil, like shallow frying or pan frying, will usually still be crisp but to a lesser extent. Other methods utilize the movement of the food in the pan or using oil or fat with other sauces. 
Frying is a dehydration process which involves the transfer of mass and heat. Different chemical changes take place during the frying process such as protein denaturation, starch gelatinization, surface browning, rapid water evaporation and oil absorption.


History
Frying is believed to have first appeared in Ancient Egyptian cuisine during the Old Kingdom, around 2500 BC. Ancient Egyptians would typically fry foods like tiger nut cakes, fish, and other foods. In the tomb of Egyptian Vizier Rekhmire, who lived in the 15th century BC, there are depictions of workers putting small cakes in pots of oil or fat and instructions in hieroglyphics to fry the food.
During the Warring States period of the Zhou dynasty (475-221 BC), the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Rites were written and contained information and recipes about the eight delicacies. The eight delicacies are recipes and culinary techniques. One of the eight delicacies is chun ao. Chun means to enrich, and ao means to fry. Chun ao is fried, pickled meat paste poured on top of upland rice mixed with rendered animal fat.
In the late 2nd century AD, Greek cook Galen describes pancake-like griddle cakes made with sesame seeds and fried in olive oil over a fire. Later, in the 5th century AD, the Roman cookbook Apicius describes a Delian sweet from the Greek island Delos. The dessert is made with hardened wheat paste that is then deep fried in oil. Commonly, the Delian sweets are covered in honey and pepper before being served.


Process
When in contact with oil heated to 150–200 °C (302–392 °F), food undergoes heat and mass transfer. The food's water content reaches boiling point and begins to vaporize, creating pores in its cell walls which enable it to absorb oil. As heat exposure is greater on the surface of the food in direct contact with the oil, water vaporization occurs more quickly. This dehydration effect causes a crisp crust to form which protects the center of the food against further oil absorption.
The crust browns due to the formation of melanoidins caused by caramelization and the Maillard reaction. The food's starch content gelatinizes, causing it to soften; the surface contains less water and retains its crisp crust. Frying is complete when all water content in the food vaporizes. When a fried food reduces in temperature below 100 °C (212 °F), water vapor inside condenses and internal pressure drops, causing oil absorption into the food via a vacuum effect.


Techniques


Air frying
In air frying, food is placed in an air fryer with a small amount of oil and then heated to an extreme temperature. Air fryers are typically considered to be a healthier alternative to frying, as they usually have less calories and a lower fat content than deep fried or shallow fried foods.


Deep frying

In deep frying, food is submerged in hot oil or fat so that all sides are cooked simultaneously. A deep fryer or chip pan may be used, or, in an industrial frying operation, a pressure fryer or vacuum fryer. One method for preparing food for deep frying involves battering or breading, which adds color and crunch to its surface. French fries, doughnuts, cong you bing, and tempura are common deep-fried foods.


Sautéing
